title: Seven Arrested After Kolkata Pandal Collapse Warning Triggered Fatal Crush
excerpt: Police say a suo motu culpable homicide case has been filed over the Chorbagan stampede that killed 19, as investigators seek to identify who announced the pandal might collapse.
body:
• Seven people have been arrested over the stampede at the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata that killed 19 people, including the puja committee secretary Rajkumar Seoda and vice-president Shantanu Dubey, The Times of India reported.
  • Police say a suo motu case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder has been filed, and investigators are examining CCTV footage to identify who announced that the pandal structure might collapse.
  • A senior Kolkata Police officer told PTI there was evidence of gross mismanagement, no clear crowd plan, and inadequate police and private security at the venue, The Hindu BusinessLine reported.
  • Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has promised a judicial probe headed by a sitting judge, subject to the chief justice's approval, or a retired judge, and said its findings will be made public.

Seven people have been arrested in connection with the stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata that killed 19 people and injured 24, after an announcement warning that the pandal structure might collapse sent visitors rushing for the exits, The Times of India reported. The crush occurred at around 7.30pm on Saptami at the Chorbagan pandal amid heavy rain. Several people fell down stairs near the exit and were trampled, and one of the injured remains in a critical condition.

The Arrests

Police arrested puja committee secretary Rajkumar Seoda and vice-president Shantanu Dubey, two of the seven held. The others were Biplab Mukhopadhyay, who was responsible for installing the bamboo structure, crowd managers Kaushik Saha and Pintu De, and private security agency employees Suman Chakraborty and Rajesh Pal, The Times of India reported. Two of those arrested are office-bearers of the Chorbagan Durga Puja committee.

A suo motu case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder was filed. A senior officer said investigators had evidence of gross mismanagement. "There was no clear plan to manage the large number of visitors, and everything was handled verbally," the officer said. An arrest does not establish guilt.

The arrests drew a divided political response. Trinamool, CPM and Congress representatives gathered at Girish Park police station to demand accountability. West Bengal Congress president Subhankar Sarkar and Trinamool MLA Kunal Ghosh called the arrests an "eyewash", while BJP Bengal president Samik Bhattacharya appealed against political recriminations, saying the priority should be supporting bereaved families.

How the Crush Happened

The crush followed a sudden downpour during Saptami celebrations. According to The Times of India, an announcement allegedly warning that the pandal's structure might collapse sent visitors rushing for the exits. Resident Ramji Sau said: "People panicked when organisers started announcing that the pandal might cave in. That caused the stampede." Another resident, Beauty Naskar, alleged there were hardly any police or volunteers controlling the crowd, with some young volunteers busy on their phones.

The Hindu BusinessLine, citing PTI, reported a senior officer said lack of crowd management and misleading announcements may have triggered the panic, and that police and private security deployed were inadequate. "People tried to escape through the entrance gate during the stampede. Both the gates and the approach road were narrow," the officer said.

Police have video footage of an announcement asking people to leave on the grounds that the structure was about to collapse, and are trying to identify who made it, the officer said. Locals claimed personnel were mainly stationed near the VIP entrance. Adhikari said temporary home guards managing ropes separating entry and exit routes abandoned their posts when the rain began.

The Investigation

A special investigation team is examining CCTV footage and eyewitness accounts to establish who made the collapse announcement and why, The Times of India reported. Forensic experts visited the pandal on Saturday night, a further team was due on Sunday, and police plan to question survivors, The Hindu BusinessLine reported.

Adhikari promised a judicial probe headed by a sitting judge, subject to the chief justice's approval, or a retired judge, and pledged to make its findings public. He announced Rs 5 lakh for each injured person. The Hindu BusinessLine reported he also announced Rs 25 lakh and a Group D government job for the family of each person who died, and ordered a Special Investigation Team headed by a sitting judge of the Calcutta High Court.

Kolkata Police Commissioner Ajay Kumar Nand imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 on roads adjoining the pandal on Sunday, in force until October 20, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. Adhikari directed police across Bengal to inspect major pandals and enforce safety measures, and nine IPS officers have been assigned puja duty in the city. Other committees moved to clear exits and limit visitors, with Santosh Mitra Square adopting staggered entry and Thakurpukur SB Park cutting its permitted crowd from about 200-250 to about 100 at a time, The Times of India reported.
